blocks.prompt: 8. Find the integer \(b\) such that the average value of \(f(x) = 2 + 4x - 3x^{2}\) on the interval \([2, b]\) equals \(-7\).
blocks.explanation:
An average-value equation with an unknown end point.
Plan: write \(\frac{1}{b-2}\int_2^b f(x)\,dx = -7\), integrate, clear the fraction and solve the cubic; keep only \(b > 2\).
steps:
Given: \(f(x) = 2 + 4x - 3x^{2}\), average on \([2, b]\) is \(-7\).
To find: the integer \(b\).
Method: \(f_{\text{av}} = \frac{1}{b-2}\int_{2}^{b} f(x)\,dx\); for \([2, b]\) to be an interval we need \(b > 2\).

Set up the equation
\[\dfrac{2b + 2b^{2} - b^{3} - 4}{b - 2} = -7\]
\[2b + 2b^{2} - b^{3} - 4 = -7b + 14\]
\[b^{3} - 2b^{2} - 9b + 18 = 0\]
Why: multiply by \(b - 2\) and move all terms to one side.

Choose the right root
\(b = 2\) gives an interval of length 0 (we divided by \(b - 2\)); \(b = -3\) is less than 2, so \([2, b]\) would not be an interval. Hence \(b = 3\).
